turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the primary business objectives and success criteria for the shared TACHOnet service, and which outcomes are most important to achieve first?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The main business objective is to give participating card-issuing authorities a reliable shared coordination service so they can check card request status across borders without each organization having to chase others separately. Success means requests are answered in a standardized way, status is visible through to completion, access is controlled properly, and overdue replies are flagged so cases do not stall.
What matters most first is making the core request-and-reply flow work consistently, because that is the operational heart of the service. After that, the priority is tracking deadlines and late responses, then access management, and finally the reporting and statistics so the organizations can monitor how well the network is performing.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which stakeholder roles or participating organizations will use, operate, administer, or receive outputs from the TACHOnet service, and what responsibilities does each role have?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The main users are the European card-issuing authorities that participate in the network, since they will send requests and receive standardized replies about card delivery or status. There will also be operational administrators for the shared service who manage access rights, monitor overdue replies, and keep the coordination service running smoothly. On top of that, management or oversight users may receive the operational statistics and status reports, but I’m not sure yet whether those are separate people or part of the same organizations’ back-office teams.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Beyond the core request-and-reply flow, deadline tracking, access control, and reporting, what specific functions should the TACHOnet service provide from end to end—for example, request submission, routing to one or more member organizations, reply tracking, notifications, case follow-up, and completion handling?
turns.interviewee_utterance: End to end, I’d expect it to let a user create and submit a request, send it to one or more selected member organizations, and then track each individual reply against that case. It should notify the sender when replies arrive or when a response is late, and keep the case open until all expected answers are back or the requester closes it. Once finished, it should store the outcome so the full history can be reviewed later.

turns.interviewer_utterance: When a request needs to be sent to one or more member organizations, how should the service determine which members to route it to, and are there any rules for sequencing, parallel delivery, retries, or excluding certain members?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The service should route based on the member or members the requester selects, using the network’s authorized participant list rather than trying to infer the target automatically. My understanding is that delivery to multiple members would usually be in parallel, because the goal is to get responses efficiently, but I’d need to confirm whether any cases require a sequence instead. I don’t know the exact retry or exclusion rules yet, though I would expect the service to avoid sending to members that are not currently active or not authorized for that type of request.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Could you define the full request lifecycle and the rules for standardized replies—for example, what status states a request should move through from submission to completion, what each member’s reply must contain or how it should be formatted, and exactly what conditions allow a case to be closed?
turns.interviewee_utterance: A request would normally move from submitted to sent, then to awaiting reply, and then to completed once all expected responses are in, or to closed if it is cancelled or otherwise terminated. Each reply should come back in a standardized format so the requesting authority can reliably read the status, the result, and any supporting message or reference data; the exact fields would need to follow the TACHOnet message definition, which I don’t have in front of me. A case can be closed when all required replies have been received, or if the requester decides no further follow-up is needed, but I’d want to verify whether there are any mandatory waiting periods before closure.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Before a requester is allowed to close a case early, are there any mandatory waiting periods or minimum time windows that must elapse, and if so what are the exact rules for when closure is permitted or blocked?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I don’t have the exact waiting-period rules confirmed yet, so I can’t state a fixed minimum time window with confidence. My expectation is that closure would be blocked while any required reply is still within its allowed response deadline, and only permitted once the requester has either received all expected responses or is explicitly allowed to abandon the case. If there are mandatory grace periods or legal retention windows, those would need to be checked with the business owners or the message specification.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Can you define the standardized TACHOnet reply message structure in more detail—what fields are required versus optional, what each field should represent, and whether there are any specific validation, code-set, or reference-data rules we need to follow?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I can’t define the exact TACHOnet reply structure from memory, because that has to match the formal interface specification and code lists used by the network. In general, I would expect required fields for the case or request identifier, the responding member, the response status, the timestamp, and any result or reason code, with optional free-text comments or supporting references. The validation rules should enforce the agreed code sets and formats very strictly so every member can process replies consistently, but I’d need to verify the exact field names and allowed values against the standard.
